kit.strength: Storm Bolt and Dwarf Toss are easy to use and Avatar makes him hard to kill.
kit.weak: Weak wave clear and falls off if his stuns miss.

attack.note: His baseline quest, Give 'em the Axe!, Skullcracker, Bronzebeard Rage and Unstoppable Force all work through basic attacks, so he fights by sticking to a stunned or slowed target.

poke.note: Storm Bolt is a 110 damage slow projectile with a short delay. Good for a stun pick, not a repeatable poke.

damage.note: Damage is modest (1414 per minute measured, siege 1835 which is the lowest of this group). Thunder Clap, Thunder Strike and Bronzebeard Rage add area and single target damage. Bronzebeard Rage heals 75 percent of damage dealt, so healing reduction hurts him.

good_into.why: Thunder Clap with Reverberation cuts attack speed by 50 percent and Imposing Presence does the same passively, which shuts down melee and basic attack heroes. Dwarf Block stops 3 hits.
Storm Bolt (1.25 second stun) piercing with the baseline quest and Haymaker (319 damage plus a 40 second cooldown stun) pick off a backline hero, with a mage behind him.
Heroes without a dodge are easy to hit with Storm Bolt and Heavy Impact (80 percent slow), so his stun and Thunder Burn always land.
Imposing Presence slows summons and Perfect Storm resets Storm Bolt when a summon dies. Sledgehammer deals 500 percent to summons and monsters.

bad_into.why: The guide says he cannot peel from high mobility heroes (Tracer) and Storm Bolt is easy to dodge on them. Dwarf Toss is his only escape.
Crowd control that lands during Dwarf Toss (E.T.C. Face Melt) kills him because it is his only escape. Hardened Shield exists for this reason.
Second Wind only works after 4 seconds without damage and he becomes mana starved in long fights. Constant chip means he never regenerates.
He has one ranged tool (Storm Bolt) and a cooldown of 10 seconds. Kiters just walk away from Thunder Clap.

wants_from_team: mage or burst that follows Storm Bolt (Li-Ming)
a second crowd control source to chain with
healer is not required because of Second Wind and Stoneform
gives_team: ranged stun pick
early vision and harassment
attack speed reduction against basic attackers
Haymaker peel or Avatar tankiness
weaknesses: Dwarf Toss is the only escape and can be interrupted
weak to percent damage while in Avatar
mana runs out in long fights
low siege and wave clear
can not peel mobile heroes

kit.strength: Spawn Egg and Safety Bubble make him a hard to remove split pusher and pest.
kit.weak: Very weak in fights and relies on baiting.

attack.note: Slime and Pufferfish are the damage. Autos matter only with Time to Krill and Toxic Buildup, which are situational talents against melee teams.

poke.note: Slime is a quick area slow and Pufferfish explodes after 2.75 seconds. Both are easy to step out of or kill, so they zone more than they kill.

damage.note: Slime does 86 then 210 to slimed targets and Pufferfish does 330, which is a lot but avoidable. Octo-Grab is a 3 second targeted stun that guarantees the Pufferfish and gives the team a kill window. His own damage in fights is below average (about 1420 hero damage per minute), while siege (7620) and experience (1225) are the highest in the league.

good_into.why: Octo-Grab stuns a target for 3 seconds with Unstoppable, so a low health priority target dies when the team follows up.
Pufferfish and Slime clear waves instantly, March of the Murlocs forces a response, and Spawn Egg makes it costly to chase him.
Spawn Egg gives a quick free return and enemies feed him a small 25 percent experience, so chip damage trades poorly for them.
Slime Time, Black Lagoon and Toxic Buildup are easiest to complete against heroes who must stay close.

bad_into.why: He has the lowest health pool of any hero, and a burst assassin can kill him before Safety Bubble matters.
Ranged heroes with mobility avoid Slime and Pufferfish and do not give him quest stacks.
Coin, gem and warhead objectives are dropped on death, so he is a poor carrier.

wants_from_team: Teammates who call and follow up on his Octo-Grab target
Damage mitigation (shields, armor, blinds)
Double soak maps and late game objectives
A team that can fight 4v5 while he soaks
gives_team: Waveclear and siege that frees the team to fight
A 3 second stun for picks
Experience and soak that drains the enemy
Egg vision that reveals stealth
weaknesses: Extremely fragile, the lowest health in the game
Weak early game
Poor on collect objectives
Damage can be avoided by playing defensively
profile.owner_notes: A split pusher with a low death timer when his egg is safe. Octo Grab can pick people. Like Samuro he wants to push side lanes and does best with siege and structure damage while pulling attention and escaping. Struggles against Ragnaros and others who can kill him for stacks or quests, or kill his W so it does not trigger.

kit.strength: Zombie Wall, Corpse Spiders and Gargantuan give excellent wave clear.
kit.weak: Slow and a poor team fighter without setup.

attack.note: Basic attacks apply Voodoo Ritual poison to minions and, after Vile Infection, to Heroes. Most of his value comes from abilities that put damage over time on a target.

poke.note: Plague of Toads is slow and easy to walk away from, but each toad stacks damage over 6 seconds, and it pressures anyone channeling an objective. Corpse Spiders are immune to damage and chase the target for 4 seconds, so that part is hard to avoid once the jar lands.

damage.note: Almost all of his damage is spread over time: toads over 6 seconds, spiders attacking for 4 seconds, Zombie Wall ticks, Ring of Poison and Vile Infection poison. A strong sustained or AoE healer undoes a lot of it, which is why Annihilating Spirit adds a 50 percent healing reduction on Ravenous Spirit. Measured siege damage of 7013 per minute is the highest of this batch and shows his real value is pushing, waveclear and objective pressure, with hero damage only around the league median at 2761.

good_into.why: Toads and spiders stack chip damage that a single target burst healer cannot spread across the team, and Pandemic reduces enemy damage by up to 25 percent.
Superstition gives 40 Spell Armor and his large maximum Health pool from Voodoo Ritual makes him a poor target to poke, while his own toads outrange most melee.
Gargantuan tanks tower shots and Toads of Hugeness plus Voodoo Ritual push, giving the highest siege damage per minute measured in this set.
He clears waves faster than almost any hero with Corpse Spiders and Plague of Toads, so he wins lanes and keeps pressure with Voodoo Ritual stacks growing.
All three toads start on him, so melee heroes that walk up take burst from every toad, and Zombie Wall ring blocks melee approach paths.

bad_into.why: He has no mobility and Ravenous Spirit is a stationary channel, so a diver can interrupt it. Only Ice Block saves him.
His damage is dot based and small per tick, so AoE healers like Brightwing or Malfurion erase it, unless he picks Annihilating Spirit.
Plague of Toads is slow and Zombie Wall is jumped or dodged by heroes with a leap, so mobile targets avoid his damage.
Stuns and silences cancel Ravenous Spirit and his Zombie Wall can be knocked back, so he loses the Heroic.
Kiters outrange the slow toads and spiders are only active 4 seconds, so a competent kiter takes little.

wants_from_team: Two lanes that are safe to rotate between so he can stack Voodoo Ritual
A frontline or crowd control to hold targets for spiders and Zombie Wall
Peel against divers because he has no escape except Ice Block
A long game so Vile Infection and Big Voodoo are online
gives_team: Elite waveclear and siege push
Zone control with Zombie Wall and Gargantuan
Heavy objective pressure from range
Healing reduction on Ravenous Spirit with Annihilating Spirit
weaknesses: No mobility and a weak escape
Slow projectiles and a stationary Heroic channel
Poor on maps with two lanes or slow rotations
Low damage taken per minute shows he relies on being protected
profile.owner_notes: A sustain damage mage with some burst from Ravenous Spirit or the spider build. No escape except a late talent Ice Block that only delays. Depends on skillshots, weaker in competitive play and stronger against uncoordinated teams. Good at wave clear and camp clear.

kit.strength: Snipe and Permanent Cloak give strong pick potential from range.
kit.weak: Highly dependent on landing Snipe and easy to punish.

attack.note: Basic attacks matter through One in the Chamber (65 percent extra after an ability) or Anti-Armor Shells (250 percent damage and armor shred), but the core is Snipe and Triple Tap, which are abilities.

poke.note: Snipe deals 230 damage from long range but is a straight projectile that dies to any body in the way and resets her stacks on a miss. Pinning Shot is unmissable but weak. Triple Tap is a locked on channel but its slow shots are blocked by structures and allies.

damage.note: Her damage comes as big single target hits: Snipe stacks to 55 percent extra, Triple Tap does 3 times 372, Precision Strike 435 in an area. Healing cannot undo that, so healers do little against her except pre shielding. The measured 2627 hero damage per minute is only a bit above league median, because she spends long periods in stealth walking, which makes her an assassin with a modest damage per minute but high kill pressure (12.5 takedowns per game).

good_into.why: Snipe at long range from stealth plus Triple Tap or Precision Strike can delete a low Health Hero that has no way to block the line.
Snipe is a straight projectile and Precision Strike has a 1.5 second delay, so stationary or slow targets eat every hit and keep her Precision Sniper stacks.
Her damage arrives in single big hits and Crippling Shot adds 20 percent damage taken, so AoE healing over time does not keep targets up.
Fragile ranged heroes expose themselves in lane, and Permanent Cloak lets her find isolated ones and Snipe them. The guide notes the psychological pressure of a stealth pick on them.
Holo Decoy blocks or defuses summon style skillshots and traps, and Precision Strike clears minions from global range.

bad_into.why: She has no mobility, only Ghost Protocol, so a diver that finds her through the shimmer kills her. The guide calls her extremely weak to dive.
Assassins with gap closers reach her faster than Pinning Shot can slow them and her Health pool is low.
Mobile heroes dodge Snipe and each miss resets Precision Sniper stacks to zero.
Any stun interrupts the stationary Triple Tap channel and she has no unstoppable tool.
Her single shots get blocked by a frontline, and with no wave clear she cannot do much when a team simply stands in front.

wants_from_team: Crowd control to make Snipe and Precision Strike land
A team that can fight while she roams and picks off isolated targets
Wave clear and camp help because she has little of either
A frontline between her and enemy divers
gives_team: Global Precision Strike for follow up and structure finishing
Stealth pressure that makes the enemy play defensively
High single target burst to kill key backliners
Holo Decoy to block skillshots such as Hook or a trap
weaknesses: No mobility or real escape
Very weak wave and camp clear
Burst resets on a missed Snipe
Reliant on allied crowd control
profile.owner_notes: A burst ranged assassin focused on pick kills. Weak without much sustain, but strong when the player is good and ganks the offlaner or vulnerable heroes.

kit.strength: Shadow Waltz, Chomp and Crushing Jaws provide pick damage with sustain.
kit.weak: Fragile and punished by CC.

attack.note: She has a ranged auto but wants to hit with it on purpose: Overflowing Chaos makes the basic attack after a hit deal 50 percent more per stack and heal for all of it. Her main damage, Chomp, has very short reach, so she fights close to the target.

poke.note: Dread is a long range, delayed wave plus eruption that slows, and Shadow Waltz is a 0.5 second cast line. Neither is reliable poke because she is built to commit with Shadow Waltz dash into Chomp, not to trade from afar.

damage.note: Shadow Waltz recasts every 2 seconds on a Hero hit, Chomp hits for 305, and Dead Magic autos ignore armor. She trades with healing by healing herself from Chaos autos. Enemy healing matters less than enemy crowd control, because a single stun cancels her Chomp and dash, as the guide says. Measured 2926 hero damage per minute is above median and 5.0 merc camps per game is the highest of this set.

good_into.why: Dead Magic autos ignore Armor and Engulfing Oblivion removes 50 Armor with Crushing Jaws, so Warriors and armored Tanks like Mal'Ganis, E.T.C. and Garrosh melt, and her Chaos heals fully.
Melee heroes have to walk into Chomp range, Invasive Miasma heals her as they stand beside her and Backbiter moves her away after a hit.
Her damage is spread across Waltz and Chomp cooldowns on one target and a single target burst healer cannot cover it, while her own healing outlasts theirs.
Crushing Jaws pull then Chomp and Shadow Waltz can solo a squishy that is caught, and Lurking Terror chases high range backliners.
Chomp and Eternal Feast hit stationary or rooted targets for the full multiple hits, as the guide says to use Eternal Feast on immobilized enemies.

bad_into.why: The guide says any crowd control greatly reduces her damage and survivability: stuns cancel Shadow Waltz and the dash, and the cast time of Chomp is easy to interrupt.
Chomp needs proximity and the guide calls the Chomp build terrible against high range enemies, so a kiter simply retreats.
Enemy backliners poke her down while she has to dash in, and her only range tool Dread is slow and avoidable.
Dive kills her before Chaos heals matter, because Shadow Waltz is a 0.5 second cast and she has no escape beyond the dash.

Her sustained trading needs a target to drop, and an AoE healer such as Brightwing or Stukov heals back the Shadow Waltz and Dread chip faster than it lands, so she needs Crushing Jaws to break through.

wants_from_team: Crowd control to set up Crushing Jaws and Chomp
A roaming group, since she is strongest next to other heroes
An XP lead, because she snowballs from it
A frontline that keeps enemy melee off her
gives_team: Pull and 0.5 second stun with Crushing Jaws
Strong camp clearing and lane presence
Armor ignoring damage into tanks
Area denial with Eternal Feast
weaknesses: Collapses to any hard crowd control
Short reach on her best ability
Weak at siege and at objective control from range
Relies on allied crowd control
profile.owner_notes: A burst mage at medium range with a high skill ceiling: she has to get close and is weak when she misses her Q. A lot of damage, some boss and area control. Her heroic resets if it hits a hero, which works well with a CC heroic such as E.T.C. Mosh Pit or Leoric Entomb.

kit.strength: Warp In Pylon, Photon Cannon and Warp Rift create strong siege and defense.
kit.weak: Needs lots of setup and loses to dive.

attack.note: He has no real basic attack value. Damage comes from Disruption Pulse, Warp Rift explosions and Photon Cannons that he warps in.

poke.note: Disruption Pulse has a 3 second cooldown and goes through everything, and Warp Rift sits on the ground as a slow field that he can detonate. Photon Cannon always targets a Hero and soaks structure shots. Players can avoid Warp Rift by walking around it.

damage.note: Rift plus Pulse is a heavy AoE burst, Null Gate and cannons do small chip damage over time, and Pylon Overcharge hits for 96 per second. Healers handle the chip, not the Rift burst. Measured siege damage of 7939 per minute is the highest of this batch and hero damage 3071 is above median. Healing 512 per minute in the measured block comes from Shield Battery, an ally shield, so he is not a healer.

good_into.why: Null Gate slows by 80 percent and Warp Rift slows by 25 percent, and Photon Cannons target Heroes, so melee heroes are held outside while he hits them.
Photon Cannons tank tower and fort fire, and Pylon Overcharge together with Rift explosions gives the top measured siege damage.
A single Disruption Pulse into Warp Rift clears a wave and Probius can solo lane well, as the guide says, which lets him run lanes and rotate on pings.
Pylon Overcharge and Gate Keeper make objective areas hard for the enemy to stand on, as the guide calls his objective control great.
Pylons give him unlimited Mana regeneration in the Power Field and Shield Capacitor and Shield Battery give shields, so he can outlast chip.

bad_into.why: The guide says he suffers against any hero that can reach him, because he needs Pylons and cannons set up and has little burst of his own.
Divers jump the Pylon or Probius before cannons come online, and Worker Rush breaks on damage.
Longer range heroes destroy undefended Pylons and he cannot outtrade with only Pulse at medium range.
Warp Rift and Null Gate are ground zones and mobile heroes walk or blink around them.
He has no stun and no escape, so crowd control makes him a free kill when Pylons are down.

wants_from_team: A frontline to keep enemy melee off his Pylons
Objectives on maps with narrow paths, which suit Null Gate
A teammate who can follow Warp Rift slows with crowd control
Allied heroes that benefit from Aggressive Matrix or Power Overflowing
gives_team: Excellent wave clear that frees the team for objectives
Zoning with Null Gate and Warp Rift
Siege pressure from Pylon Overcharge and cannons
Shields and Spell Power in the Power Field
weaknesses: Needs Pylons and mana setup
Very exposed to anything that reaches him
Situational and a high skill ceiling
Win rate 0.481 over only 54 games
profile.owner_notes: Setup dependent because he needs Pylons around him. Dies to dive or CC and is weaker in the current meta.

kit.strength: Grappling Hook and Revolving Sweep make her a mobile duelist who is hard to catch.
kit.weak: Very poor wave clear and dependent on terrain.

attack.note: Basic attacks and every ability apply Blood Rage's stackable bleed, and Finishing Touch, The Hunted and Siphoning Link make autos a real damage and heal source. Carnage is a short range piercing line so she stays close to targets.

poke.note: Carnage and Grappling Hook apply bleed from a short distance but she wants contact; the bleed itself is applied by landing slow skillshots.

damage.note: Most damage is a stacking bleed (28 over 4 seconds, 5 stacks, with a permanent quest bonus) that is refreshed on every hit. Enemy healing can offset it, but she spreads bleed across several heroes and Final Strike (410, plus 25 percent under 50 percent health) and Fatal Wounds finish low targets. Blood Rage also heals her in proportion to the number of bled heroes.

good_into.why: Grappling Hook and Revolving Sweep reach a flanked target and Final Strike executes low health heroes.
Bleed ignores part of the armor math and Lingering Ailment shreds 25 armor, so she out damages tanks over time.
Upstage evades heroic basic attacks and Revolving Sweep makes her immune to damage, so she wins duels.
Single target healers cannot out heal the stacked, refreshed bleed spread across several heroes.

bad_into.why: Every ability except Blood Rage can be interrupted by stuns, silences or displacement, and Unrelenting Strikes is stopped by them too.
Carnage and Revolving Sweep are slow skillshots, so mobile ranged heroes like Tracer avoid the whole kit.
AoE healers (Brightwing, Lucio, Malfurion) undo spread bleed, and she lacks burst to finish through that.
Needs vision for a skillshot kit and for No Sanctuary reveals, so stealth heroes make it hard to stack bleeds.

wants_from_team: Hard CC from a tank to land her skillshots
A single target healer or damage buffer
Terrain and open maps with flank routes
Wave clear from the team since hers is weak
gives_team: A flank and execute threat
Strong solo lane pressure
Spread damage over time on several enemies
A 1.5 second stun with Unrelenting Strikes in the right comp
weaknesses: Poor waveclear
Depends on terrain for Grappling Hook
Susceptible to stuns and silences
High death count and a steep learning curve

kit.strength: Empower Sulfuras, Living Meteor and Lava Wave make him one of the best sieging heroes.
kit.weak: No mobility and weak when caught by dive.

attack.note: Melee basic attacks, but Empower Sulfuras makes the next attack an instant splash ability that heals, and Blistering Attacks adds bonus damage to attacks. Living Meteor gives a ranged option and Sulfuras Smash has very long range.

poke.note: Living Meteor is a vector skillshot that rolls 1.75 seconds and relies on enemies walking along it, so good players sidestep it. Molten Core Meteor Shower and Explosive Rune (large range) are extra poke on a few maps.

damage.note: Most damage is repeated AoE chip: Empower Sulfuras splash every 4 seconds, Living Meteor ticks, Blast Wave. Sulfuras Smash adds a burst (594 center plus stun) and Giant Scorcher adds 9 percent max health burn. Measured hero damage 2076 per minute is about the median while siege damage 10026 per minute is more than double the median.

cc.note: Sulfuras Smash stuns for 0.5 seconds in the center and is a telegraphed 0.75 second delay. Slow Burn, Meteor Shower and Flames of Sulfuron add slows. Molten Swing stuns and knocks back but only inside Molten Core. Measured CC on enemies 2.7 seconds per game, very low.

good_into.why: Empower Sulfuras hits everything near the target and Hand of Ragnaros refunds mana and speeds its cooldown when two heroes are hit. Melee heroes cannot avoid the splash and fight at his range.
Molten Core turns an allied or destroyed fort into a 5000 health body with extended range that defends structures and pokes the capture area, plus he double soaks on maps like Infernal Shrines.
All his abilities are AoE and he clears minions and summons cheaply with Living Meteor and Empower Sulfuras.
Giant Scorcher burns 9 percent of max health and Sulfuras Smash center deals large flat damage, so big health pools are not wasted on him.
Lava Wave kills minions instantly and soaks experience without exposing him, and Lava Surge sends minions down faster. Gives global value on large maps.

bad_into.why: He has no gap closer (Blast Wave is only a short speed boost) and the guide says he is extremely weak to kite. Living Meteor is dodgeable.
Ranged heroes outrange Empower Sulfuras and make him fight at the edge of his reach where only Living Meteor works.

His basic abilities and Empower Sulfuras are channels or instant attacks that do not protect him, and the guide names Sonya style interrupts as a problem. Resilient Flame only helps against stuns every 15 seconds.
He is not hard to kill when focused and has no escape beyond Submerge on a 60 second cooldown at level 20.
He lacks mobility to engage across the map and Molten Core can be avoided by retreating for its 18 second cooldown.

wants_from_team: Reliable crowd control to land Sulfuras Smash on a center target
A tank that creates the opening so he does not engage first
Support to hold the offlane when Molten Core is down
Maps where he can double soak
gives_team: Top tier wave clear and siege pressure
Structure defense with Molten Core
Long range stun follow up with Sulfuras Smash
Global minion clear with Lava Wave
weaknesses: No mobility
Kited easily
Weak on capture point maps with no double soak
Telegraphed burst
profile.owner_notes: A bruiser who soaks lanes well. His trait defends against a strong push or stalls near the objective. His heroic Smash does huge damage when set up with CC, and Lava Wave can clear a heavy push. Good on most wave clear maps, but on Tomb of the Spider Queen clearing waves with Lava Wave loses the gems. Low health and no escape, so he loses to other bruisers that can CC him or out sustain him.

kit.strength: Inspire, Adrenaline Rush and Hyperion give steady auto attack damage and ally buffs.
kit.weak: Low burst and easy to dive.

attack.note: He is an auto attack carry. Give 'Em Some Pepper makes every fourth basic attack hit for 125 percent more with splash, and almost every talent buffs basic attacks. He needs to stutter step between shots.

poke.note: Auto attacks and Penetrating Round are not dodgeable in the normal sense. Penetrating Round is a line that knocks back and slows, and it has a 9 second cooldown.

damage.note: Steady auto damage with a burst on every fourth attack. Healers answer it with normal healing, but Bounty Hunter adds 3 percent of maximum Health and Dusk Wing shreds armor, which beats healing on tanks. Hyperion pushes and zones rather than kills. The measured 2420 hero damage per minute is just above league median and the win rate of 0.447 over 826 games is low, so he is a common but average carry.

good_into.why: Penetrating Round knocks back and slows a line of melee heroes and cancels leaps like Avenging Wrath or Jet Propulsion, which the guide mentions.
Bounty Hunter deals 3 percent of maximum Health and Dusk Wing banshee removes up to 30 Armor, so tanks do not tank him.
Inspire speeds up minions and mercenaries, Exterminator deals 125 percent more to minions, and Hyperion fires Yamato Cannon for 794 at a structure.
Sustained auto damage with Raynor's Raider banshee on one target outlasts a single target healer's mana.
Measured 5.3 merc camps per game, the highest in the set, and Adrenaline Rush with Sustaining Rounds keeps him in lane.

bad_into.why: The guide notes he has no gap closer and lacks any escape except knockback and Adrenaline Rush, which cannot be used at full Health.
Assassins close the gap and kill him inside the 4 second window of one rotation before Penetrating Round comes back.
Stuns stop his stutter step and Adrenaline Rush, and he has Unstoppable only from Raiders Roll at level 20.
A kiter with equal or longer range keeps out of Raynor medium range, and slow Penetrating Round only slows for 2 seconds.
Mobile heroes dodge the line of Penetrating Round and he has no way to follow them.

wants_from_team: Peel and a frontline to protect him while he auto attacks
Crowd control so his slows and Bounty Hunter land consistently
Lane partners so Inspire buffs minions and mercenaries
Map objectives that Hyperion can zone
gives_team: Reliable sustained damage and wave clear
Mercenary camp clears and siege push
Knockback to peel melee
Hyperion for objective pressure and Execute Orders for a late revenge
weaknesses: No mobility or escape
Low win rate in this data
Weak at engaging
Basic attack reliance makes him easy to kite and burst

kit.strength: Ghost Wolf, Chain Heal and Lightning Shield offer heavy sustain with melee presence.
kit.weak: Moderate damage and less healing than pure healers.

attack.note: Basic attacks are short range and Ghost Wolf lunge attacks deal 60 percent bonus damage, which is how he clears camps. Hunger of the Wolf and Blood and Thunder build on wolf attacks.

poke.note: Lightning Shield deals 64 per second to nearby enemies while it is on an ally, and Earthgrasp Totem gives a 90 damage burst and near root. Real damage is vs minions and camps. Measured hero damage 669 per minute, the lowest of the group.

damage.note: The damage is area dot and is easy to heal through. It mostly clears waves and mercenary camps.

healing.note: Chain Heal bounces to three Heroes for 260 each, which is decent sustain but the guide notes limited single target sustain into poke on a lone tank. Ancestral Healing is 1180 after a 1 second delay, so the burst heal needs prediction and is blunted by healing reduction. Earth Shield and Elemental Conduit give shields to cover the delay. Farseer's Blessing makes it a second AoE heal.

good_into.why: Ancestral Healing, Earth Shield and Elemental Conduit are built for burst and Purge frees an ally from crowd control. The guide names burst compositions as his best matchup.
Earthbind Totem with Grounded Totem and Earthgrasp Totem slows melee Heroes by 90 percent for a second, cutting their attack speed and spell power in the area.
Purge on an ally gives a free 0.5 second Unstoppable on a 60 second cooldown, and Purification heals when it removes a stun, root, slow or silence.
He clears waves and camps alone with Lightning Shield and Ghost Wolf, so he can soak lanes or take camps when the enemy rotates.

bad_into.why: The guide names constant single target pressure on a tank as his weakness, because Chain Heal is moderate sustain and Ancestral Healing is a one time burst.
Short range Ghost Wolf and a small slow do not catch kiters, and his damage vs Heroes is minimal without lunging in.
Long range damage dealers hit him and his team without anything to answer back, and his Lightning Shield does nothing at range.
Ancestral Healing has a 1 second delay and if its target dies in that window he waits 10 seconds, and he has no hard crowd control or interrupt.

wants_from_team: Bruisers and melee assassins to receive Lightning Shield and Bloodlust
A frontline that can absorb damage while Chain Heal bounces
Hard crowd control, since he has none
Map pressure he can add by taking camps himself
gives_team: Mercenary camp and lane control from a healer slot
Burst protection with Ancestral Healing and shields
Bloodlust attack speed and move speed with life steal
Purge cleanse for one ally
weaknesses: No hard crowd control or interrupt
Limited single target sustain into poke
Healing reduction such as Biotic Grenade blunts Ancestral Healing
Purge range is low and Unstoppable is only 0.5 seconds
Weak in constant skirmish early
profile.owner_notes: Okay heals, nothing massive until Ancestral Healing, which is on a long cooldown. Good at camps and wave clear. His totem slows. His trait cleanses an ally or slows an enemy on a long cooldown, cannot be used on himself, and he has no escape. Good if the team lacks wave clear, weak elsewhere. A decent healer overall.

kit.strength: Misha is a strong frontline and Rexxar clears camps with ease.
kit.weak: Weak to poke and needs to manage two bodies.

attack.note: Rexxar and Misha both deal damage with basic attacks. Aspect of the Hawk, Dire Beast, Aspect of the Beast and Frenzy of Kalimdor feed from attacks, and Bestial Wrath triples Misha's attacks.

poke.note: Spirit Swoop is a line skillshot with a slow (141 damage, 7 second cooldown). Taking Flight adds range and refunds on hit. Otherwise he has no poke.

damage.note: Damage comes from two bodies auto attacking plus Misha, Charge! (150 plus Dire Beast stacks). It is neither burst nor poke. Measured damage 1883 per minute is a little under the median, so he is a control bruiser, not a damage carry. Healing on the target blunts the autos.

cc.note: Misha, Charge! is a 1.25 second stun on a 10 second cooldown (lower with Aspect of the Beast), Kill Command roots for 1.5 seconds, Unleash the Boars slows 40 percent for 5 seconds. Measured 34.5 seconds of enemy stun, root or silence per game, among the highest in the league.

good_into.why: Misha charges past and stuns retreating targets, Spirit Swoop and Unleash the Boars slow, and Thrill of the Hunt speeds both bodies. Kill Command roots for the engage.
Unleash the Boars reveals every hero it tracks, Flare reveals an area and Wildfire Bear reveals invisible units that Misha walks near.
Misha can leap behind enemies and Bestial Wrath triples her attack damage on priority targets in the backline. The charge stun also body blocks escape routes.
Misha holds a capture point while Rexxar clears minions, so he wins point control and can score gems on Tomb of the Spider Queen without losing them when only Misha dies.

bad_into.why: Mobile assassins such as Zeratul dodge Misha's charge, dive Rexxar behind Misha and kill him while Feign Death is down. The guide names this directly.
When Misha dies his takedown credit and most of his talents stop working, and enemies can pick the pet off for little cost.
Misha is a second target that takes poke damage, and Mend Pet costs a lot of mana for a heal over time. Spirit Swoop is his only range.
No mobility of his own beyond Thrill of the Hunt, so heroes with gap closers reach him behind Misha or kite him freely.

wants_from_team: Follow up burst or area damage on stunned and slowed targets
Allied crowd control or grouping (Johanna, Malfurion) to extend his engage
A team that does not need him to carry damage
Maps with a capture point objective where Misha can hold
gives_team: Frequent area stuns and slows for engage and peel
Point control and objective holding with a second body

kit.strength: Mirror Image, Wind Walk and Illusion Master are great for splitting and escaping.
kit.weak: Extremely hard to master with little team fight impact.

attack.note: Samuro and his Mirror Images deal almost all damage with critical autos (every 4th or 3rd attack and Critical Strike). He has no real damaging ability apart from Bladestorm.

poke.note: No ranged damage. He uses Wind Walk and Image Transmission to close and he is revealed by his own attacks.

damage.note: Steady crit based auto damage multiplied by images (Illusion Master doubles their damage). Healing and Biotic Armor type effects blunt it, but Harsh Winds adds burst from stealth. His role in a draft is macro: split push, clear camps, tie up defenders. Measured siege per minute (about 7050) is the second highest in the league while hero damage is below average (about 1890) and he takes little damage (1841).

good_into.why: Mirror Images soak tower shots, Bladestorm clears a wave instantly, and Wind Walk heals him so he rarely has to return to base.
Great duelist after level 7 and strong at channeling objectives with stall, so he beats most heroes sent to stop him.
Image Transmission and Harsh Winds give burst on a lone ranged hero, and Wind Walk stealth approaches unseen.
Slowed or stunned targets take guaranteed crits with Merciless Strikes, and they cannot shake him.

bad_into.why: Stukov's Biotic Armor and Flailing Swipe or any sustain healer cut his auto damage and extend fights that his images cannot win.
Knockbacks (Lucio, E.T.C.) and targeted CC stop his autos, and he has no CC of his own.
Heroes that kill images easily (Jaina, Orphea, Cassia with Surge of Light) turn his decoys into free stacks and quests for them, and clone hitters like Medivh and Diablo benefit from them.

wants_from_team: A team that does not need peel from him
A healer that can heal from afar (Malfurion, Deckard)
Stat buffs for images (Abathur style)
Teammates who can fight 4v5 while he soaks
gives_team: Strong split push and backdoor pressure
Wave and camp clear with Bladestorm
Decoys that waste enemy cooldowns
Objective stalling in duels
weaknesses: Weak early game
Vulnerable if revealed or knocked back
Images can complete enemy quests and feed healing based talents
No crowd control and very low peel
profile.owner_notes: High skill ceiling. Offlanes well and later double soaks. Hard to kill, which is his strength: he pulls attention from objectives so the team can take them, and wastes the enemy's time if they send people to gank and he still escapes.

kit.strength: Siege Mode pokes anything at long range and destroys structures.
kit.weak: Immobile and has little protection.

attack.note: She switches between a normal stance and Siege Mode, which gives 20 percent more auto damage, double range and 25 percent splash but roots her in place. Her value is almost entirely basic attacks from Siege Mode.

poke.note: Siege Mode autos reach roughly twice normal range and Graduating Range adds up to 3 more. Autos are hard to dodge, Spider Mines and Napalm Strike zone ground, but she is a sitting target while in Siege Mode.

damage.note: Steady auto damage with splash, Spider Mines and Napalm Strike are spread damage that healing handles, while Giant Killer adds 1.5 percent of maximum Health on autos and Shrapnel Mines shred armor. Blunt Force Gun is a 500 damage line burst for kills. The measured 3810 hero damage per minute is the highest in this batch, with 7190 siege damage per minute, so she is the best pure damage carry of the eight when she is left alone, at a win rate of 0.482.

good_into.why: Concussive Blast knocks back, Spider Mines slow by 25 percent and Barricade builds a wall, and Siege Mode range keeps melee at a distance.
Siege Mode autos out range towers and forts and she tops siege damage in this set, with Napalm Strike and Blunt Force Gun at 50 percent structure damage.
Giant Killer deals 1.5 percent of maximum Health per auto and Shrapnel Mines reduces armor by up to 50, so tanks lose most of their value.
Targets that cannot leave the range of Siege Mode autos and Blunt Force Gun take everything, and Executioner adds 30 percent when they are slowed.
Long range Siege Mode autos with Ambush stealth hit for 125 percent more, so a backliner who stays in view loses a lot of Health.

bad_into.why: Siege Mode roots her unless she takes Hover Siege Mode, and Thrusters is her only escape, so divers kill her. The guide says to avoid Siege Mode against heroes that can punish it.
Assassins with gap closers get through mines and Concussive Blast and her Health is low, so she dies when she cannot kite.
Siege Mode makes her a stationary target for skillshots and area of effect, such as Chromie or Jaina, and the guide warns about being vulnerable to AoE.
Stuns and roots mean Thrusters, which lasts 4 seconds, is lost and Neosteel Plating has a 16 second cooldown.
Mobile heroes dodge Blunt Force Gun and Napalm Strike, and she cannot chase them.

wants_from_team: A frontline to protect her while in Siege Mode
Crowd control and peel against divers
Allies who can hold enemies in her range
Space to siege with the team nearby
gives_team: Top siege damage and structure pressure
Zone control with mines and Napalm Strike
Long range sustained damage
A global Blunt Force Gun for finishing targets
weaknesses: Immobile in Siege Mode
One escape on a 30 second cooldown
Weak camp clear and solo play
Vulnerable to AoE and burst
profile.owner_notes: A ranged sustain damage hero who can siege from very far. Susceptible to dive and to long range poke from heroes like Tassadar, Chromie and maybe Li-Ming. If the other team does not draft to kill her she destroys buildings and dominates team fights, but she depends on draft and positioning because she cannot reposition quickly and can be locked down by CC when her unstoppable shield talent or trait is down or interrupted.

kit.strength: Leap, Whirlwind and Seismic Slam give a strong brawl with sustain.
kit.weak: Weak against kiting and sustained CC.

attack.note: Fast attack speed melee. Basic attacks generate Fury, War Paint and Giant Slammer heal from them, Shot Of Fury and Rampage empower them, and the guide recommends two attacks between each Seismic Slam.

poke.note: No ranged damage. Ancient Spear is a skillshot gap closer and stun, not poke. Composite Spear extends its range by 50 percent.

damage.note: Seismic Slam on a 1 second cooldown plus fast autos is steady single target damage, Giant Slammer adds 1.5 percent max health with 60 percent lifesteal and Wrath of the Berserker adds 40 percent damage. Measured hero damage 1719 per minute is below the 2060 median, so she is a durable duelist and lane bully rather than a big damage carry. Healing on the target blunts her only part way because she heals back.

cc.note: Ancient Spear stuns briefly if it hits, and Leap (if picked at level 10) stuns 1.25 seconds in an area. Both depend on landing. Measured 16.3 seconds of enemy CC per game.

good_into.why: Giant Slammer deals 1.5 percent of max health on every attack and slam, and Wrath of the Berserker adds 40 percent damage, so she duels tanks and bruisers well.
Whirlwind heals three times as much when it hits heroes and several melee targets stay inside it. Tough As Nails blocks work against slow hitters, and she wins duels at melee range.
Ancient Spear pulls her to the target and stuns, Fury movement speed (No Escape 20 percent) lets her stay on and Wrath makes her hard to peel.
With the Leap build, Furious Blow and Poisoned Spear give a burst window on a stunned target. This is a situational pick and not her main mode.

bad_into.why: No ranged damage and no talent for it. The guide lists susceptible to kiting first, and Composite Spear is a late answer.
She has nothing against poke, so mobile ranged damage dealers wear her down while Fury only regenerates when she is hit or attacking.
Wrath only halves stun, root and slow, not silence, fear or taunt. Whirlwind and Ancient Spear are interrupted by crowd control and a missed spear leaves her Fury starved.
Fury does not regenerate over time and her sustain needs contact, so poke drains her before the fight. Tough As Nails and Ignore Pain help little against spread chip damage.

wants_from_team: A tank or crowd control to stop kiters
Healing, mitigation or Nano style buffs to prolong Wrath of the Berserker
Burst follow up if Leap is picked
Mercenary camp maps where she can take camps for the team
gives_team: Mercenary camp control and lane pressure
Wave clear and structure damage
Self sufficient solo lane
An engage and interrupt with Leap in the situational build
weaknesses: Susceptible to kiting
No ranged damage
Whirlwind easily interrupted
Reliant on hitting Ancient Spear for Fury
profile.owner_notes: A good brawler bruiser like Thrall, better at wave clear and camps. High burst, and can jump the enemy backline with Leap, a good hero for combos behind a CC chain (Light bomb). Her other heroic gives more sustain. When the enemy has no CC her spin can deal decent damage and sustain through a lot of fights.

kit.strength: Hook is a game changing pick and Devour heals him through damage.
kit.weak: Hook is one skillshot and he cannot catch mobile heroes.

attack.note: Basic attacks apply Vile Gas and feed Vile Cleaver, Tenderizer and Chop Chop. Slam and Devour are more important than autos.

poke.note: Hook is a long range skillshot (91 damage, extended 40 percent after level 13) that is a pick tool not a poke. A Hook that misses or hits a minion wastes a 16 second cooldown.

damage.note: Damage is Vile Gas (36 over 4 seconds, 150 percent bonus against minions and camps), Slam (104) and Devour (114). That is chip damage that healing blunts, 1563 damage per minute measured. His strength is the pick, not the damage.

good_into.why: Hook pulls the first enemy from a long range and stuns them, and Gorge removes them from the fight for 4 seconds. A squishy that stands behind its frontline is a free kill with burst.
Hook is long range so ranged heroes that stay far back can still be grabbed, and Devour with Digestive Juices halves the damage of one target. Hungry Hungry Stitches can Gorge several.
Gorge near allied structures or a Gate holds a target with no escape. Heroes without a dash cannot dodge the follow up.
Master Hooker removes 75 percent of healing for 2 seconds after a Hook and Putrefaction does 40 percent with Shambling Horror, so he pulls the healer then cuts their heals.

bad_into.why: High mobility heroes dodge Hook and he has no mobility or peel to answer them. Weak peeling is listed as a weakness.
A diver reaches his backline and he cannot Hook what is already on top of his team. He has only Slam slow and Helping Hand.
A summon on the Hook line absorbs it (the guide lists this), and Hook cannot pass minions or heroes in the way.
He has one tool, so a stun that stops Hook or Devour leaves him useless. Gas Bag gives Unstoppable only at level 20.
Hook is the only way to reach them. Devour and Slam are short range and Hook is a 16 second cooldown.

wants_from_team: crowd control follow up (root, stun) on the hooked target
burst damage to kill before the enemy reacts
an offlaner who can act as a secondary tank (Blaze)
a disengage such as Mighty Gust to protect him
gives_team: long range pick that starts the fight
strong wave clear
rescue pull with Helping Hand
large health pool and heals itself
weaknesses: one dimensional, everything is Hook
no mobility
weak peel
weak to percent health damage (Leoric Drain Hope)
easy to blank by drafting high mobility heroes

kit.strength: Healing Pathogen, Weighted Pustule and Massive Shove provide poke and heal.
kit.weak: Mana heavy and fragile.

attack.note: The guide calls his basic attack very strong, and it is melee until Fetid Touch makes it ranged and slowing at 35 percent less damage.

poke.note: Lurking Arm deals 136 per second and silences everything in an area, and can be channeled indefinitely. Weighted Pustule is a slow and a delayed burst. Measured hero damage 1120 per minute.

damage.note: Silence zone denies abilities more than it deals damage. Damage from Lurking Arm is small per tick.

healing.note: Healing Pathogen is 222 over 4.5 seconds and spreads to nearby allies, and Bio-Kill Switch detonates each one for 435 instantly (30 percent more with Vigorous Reuptake at 3 or more). That gives both sustain between detonations and a very large AoE burst every 16 seconds. Pox Populi and Top Off push sustain. It needs allies grouped within spread range.

good_into.why: Healing Pathogen spreads a heal over time to the whole team and Bio-Kill Switch detonates all of it at once, covering spread chip damage and burst, and Lurking Arm zones the poke Heroes out of position.
Lurking Arm silence zone at a choke, Weighted Pustule slow, Flailing Swipe and Massive Shove remove melee Heroes from the fight, and Virulent Reaction roots them inside the zone.
Lurking Arm can be dropped on a Hero channeling a heroic to cancel it, with a low cooldown.
A channeled silence zone on a choke or objective forces the enemy to concede or push through, and Massive Shove can stun a Hero into a wall.

bad_into.why: High mobility Heroes jump over the zone and he has no mobility and no escape of his own. Massive Shove is a skillshot that mobile Heroes dodge.
He has no cleanse or Unstoppable, and a channeled Lurking Arm leaves him standing still. Superstrain only heals after the stun.
Divers skip the zone and kill a healer who has to stand with allies to spread Pathogen, though Reactive Ballistospores and Massive Shove armor give some answer.
Melee body with low health and no mobility. Reactive Ballistospores resets Bio-Kill Switch below 50 percent health but that is the only protection.

wants_from_team: Allies who fight grouped within Healing Pathogen range
Reliable crowd control to land Virulent Reaction and Growing Infestation
Heroes who like slowed targets (Executioner style)
A frontline that holds the choke while he channels
gives_team: Big AoE burst heal on a 16 second detonation
Area silence and zone control
Frequent slows
Disengage or pick with Flailing Swipe and Massive Shove
weaknesses: No mobility
Bio-Kill Switch is a long cooldown tool
No cleanse or Unstoppable
Vulnerable while channeling Lurking Arm
Needs allies grouped
profile.owner_notes: A healer who mixes sustain and burst healing but excels at neither. His strength is the AoE channelled silence. No solid escape beyond Swipes to push people back, and dive can focus him when the team has no front line. Drafted with taunt Varian or another easy to hit CC tank, he silences under the target and the team bursts the taunted target with a ranged assassin like Jaina, whose damage is quick and not blocked by minions or heroes (Greymane, Li-Ming, Kel'Thuzad, Kael'thas also work). It fails when the other team can save the target: Anduin's pull counters it, and so do Medivh or Uther Divine Shield or Tyrael's invulnerability. Cleanses help, but the silence can still get kills when the target is cleansed.

kit.strength: Black Arrows, Haunting Wave and Mind Control give strong wave clear and siege.
kit.weak: Weak to dive and low burst.

attack.note: Every basic attack stacks Black Arrows, and three stacks make her hit harder, up to 50 percent after the quest and heal with Life Drain. Withering Fire and Shadow Dagger are used to feed those stacks, so her damage is auto based.

poke.note: Withering Fire auto locks the nearest enemy Hero for 5 shots and cannot be dodged, and Shadow Dagger is a targeted poison that spreads on damage. Her range is long but the real exposure comes from needing stacks.

damage.note: Dagger poison and stacked autos are spread damage that a healer can match, but Overwhelming Affliction deals 1 percent of maximum Health on autos to slowed enemies and Life Drain gives her own healing. Barbed Shot adds a 400 percent bonus on the fifth shot. The measured 2560 hero damage per minute is above median, win rate 0.482 over 2181 games, the most played hero in this batch, so she is a standard pick with an average result.

good_into.why: Black Arrows rises to 50 percent more damage at 3 stacks, Cold Embrace removes 25 Armor from the dagger target and Overwhelming Affliction deals percent maximum Health to slowed Heroes, which tanks cannot absorb.
Haunting Arrows stuns structures, Withering Fire targets towers, and Black Arrows quest stacks come from structures, so she pushes without minions.
Shadow Dagger spreads poison to nearby enemies including summons and Unstable Poison explodes minions, so she clears them quickly.
Single healers cannot keep up with Dagger spread plus fully stacked autos, and Life Drain heals her in return.
Windrunner and Will of the Forsaken give her escapes, and Wailing Arrow silences the enemies who would hold crowd control, so she has answers in her kit.

bad_into.why: Haunting Wave is her only escape and has an 11 second cooldown and 75 Mana, so a diver that kills her in one rotation wins.
Assassins with gap closers reach her through the teleport, and her Health is low.
She needs 3 stacks on one target, so mobile heroes that break line of sight reset stacks, and Shadow Dagger must hit its original target.
Her damage is spread across stacks and Dagger poison, which AoE healers erase, until the Black Arrows quest finishes.
She has no reliable burst and must stand and attack to stack, so heavy poke on her costs her the stacks and Mana.

wants_from_team: A frontline that keeps enemies at 3 stacks
Time to complete the Black Arrows quest, which makes her a mid to late game hero
Peel against divers, because Haunting Wave is her only escape
Map objectives where her stacks can be maintained on structures
gives_team: Strong wave clear and camp clear
Silence from Wailing Arrow and forced movement from Mind Control
Damage scaling against tanks and structures
Pushing power without minions
weaknesses: Quest dependent damage
One escape and low Health
Needs many basic attacks, so she is stationary
Win rate 0.482 shows no standout strength

kit.strength: Force Wall, Shock Ray and Archon provide poke and peel for allies.
kit.weak: Lower damage early and Archon is a commitment.

attack.note: Resonance Beam is a channeled slowing beam that ramps damage and mana regen, but the real value is Shock Ray and Psionic Storm. Arc Discharge adds range and Archon turns autos into the main damage source.

poke.note: Psionic Storm is instant, huge radius and long range (Psi-Infusion adds 33%), so it is hard to avoid when enemies group. Shock Ray is a narrow channel that mobile heroes sidestep, and any knockback or stun cancels it.

damage.note: Every ability is area damage. Psionic Storm ramps up to double damage the longer a target stays in it, so enemies that stand still take a lot, and enemies that step out take little. Shock Ray and Black Hole are real burst, but the bulk is a repeated area zone that healers can undo partly.

good_into.why: Psionic Storm and Shock Ray outrange most heroes, so he wins the long range trade and can zone choke points before a fight starts.
Melee heroes must walk through Psionic Storm, which ramps up to double damage, and Shock Ray slows them; Force Wall can cut off the engage.
Slow targets cannot step out of Psionic Storm or sidestep Shock Ray, so every ability lands in full.
Measured siege is about 6400 per minute against a league median near 4430, driven by Psionic Storm and Shock Ray on waves and forts.
Psionic Storm hits whole wave and summon clusters for area damage and clears minion screens cheaply.

bad_into.why: He has no escape outside Shadow Walk, low health, and Shock Ray is a channel that a diver simply ignores.
Fast heroes dodge Shock Ray and leave Psionic Storm before it ramps, and Icy Veins notes all his abilities are easy to dodge.
Stuns, silences and knockbacks cancel Shock Ray and Archon time, and he has no way to cleanse.
Psionic Storm ticks and slow beam damage are spread, so a strong sustain healer can offset the chip.
A coordinated dive removes a squishy immobile target before Archon or Black Hole come online.

wants_from_team: A tank or hard CC hero (E.T.C., Johanna style) to hold enemies in Psionic Storm and Shock Ray
Peel from the frontline because he cannot escape
A mobile assassin to finish low health targets he slows
Safe positions behind choke points
gives_team: Elite wave clear so teammates can rotate
Long range zone control at choke points and objectives
Force Wall to split an engage or save an ally
Archon spell armor shred of 20 for team burst
weaknesses: Very squishy and immobile
Mana hungry unless Resonance Beam is kept charged
Force Wall is hard to use and can hurt his own team
Needs level 10 Archon to fight straight up

kit.strength: Ruthless Onslaught and Lamb to the Slaughter give heavy single target dive.
kit.weak: Poor sustain and he is easy to kite.

attack.note: Fresh Meat adds up to 125 attack damage and 25 percent attack speed, and Butcher's Brand heals only through autos on the branded target. Hamstring resets the next auto.

poke.note: No poke. Hamstring is a short slow line and everything else needs contact.

damage.note: Late game Fresh Meat autos hit extremely hard and Brand heals him 75 percent (double on heroes) of damage dealt, so sustained healing is hard to out heal. Furnace Blast (500, three second delay) or Lamb to the Slaughter gives pick burst. Measured hero damage per minute (about 1520) is far below the median, so in NGS he is a gank and pick hero with a short fight window rather than a damage leader.

good_into.why: Ruthless Onslaught makes him Unstoppable to reach and stun a target, then Furnace Blast kills assassins and healers from full health.
Early roaming for Fresh Meat and Lamb to the Slaughter chains a lone hero so his team gets an easy kill.
Lamb to the Slaughter silences blinks and dashes, and Flail Axe with Crippling Slam keeps the Hamstring slow on mobile targets.
Targets with no escape under Butcher's Brand give him full heals and cannot disengage.

bad_into.why: Stuns, silences and blinds stop his autos and Brand healing, and Johanna's blind is called out in the guide as a hard counter.
Focus fire kills him after Ruthless Onslaught because he has no mobility or defensive tools beyond Meat Shield and Enraged.
Armored tanks and multiple supports blunt Furnace Blast and Lamb to the Slaughter and he cannot reach the backline.
Stasis, cleanses and invulnerability (Brightwing, Jaina, Whitemane, Tyrael, Johanna) negate both heroics.

wants_from_team: Hard CC to follow Ruthless Onslaught
Damage mitigation after he commits (Uther, Medivh)
Allies who protect him from focus fire
A roaming, gank oriented composition
gives_team: A hard engage and pick
Lamb to the Slaughter chain lockdown, even late
Heavy single target burst on a squishy
Early gank pressure
weaknesses: Extremely vulnerable to burst and crowd control including blinds
Both heroics can be negated by many abilities
Loses Fresh Meat on death before the quest is done
Needs a composition built around him

kit.strength: Three bodies, Longboat Raid and Viking Hoard create map control.
kit.weak: Must be micromanaged and has low team fight power.

attack.note: Three bodies: Olaf is melee, Baleog and Erik are ranged. Almost every part of the damage is basic attacks (Fury of the Storm, Nordic Attack Squad, Impatience Is a Virtue). Spin To Win! is the one ability and it hits every Viking at once.

poke.note: No poke. Erik harasses channeled objectives with his long attack range, which is interruption, not damage.

damage.note: Hero damage is small (1498 per minute) but siege is the highest in the game (8414 per minute, league median 4430) and experience is 1666. Nordic Attack Squad deals 1.25 percent of max health so it ignores healing less than flat chip does, but three small bodies are easy for healers to ignore. The value is lane pressure, not kills.

good_into.why: Heroes without a dash cannot catch three bodies with Go Go Go! (30 percent speed), Jump! (1.5 seconds Invulnerable) and Erik's speed, and they cannot stop a lane being pushed.
Nordic Attack Squad does bonus damage as a percent of maximum health, and Spin To Win! deals 100 percent more to heroes, so big health pools are what they hit best.
Erik cancels altar and tribute channels, Viking Bribery takes camps in seconds and Play Again! lets them over extend. The 4v5 fights are won by the experience lead.

bad_into.why: Zeratul and Nova kill a Viking from stealth and each Viking has a tiny health pool. The guide lists them as the main counters. Single target burst (Falstad) also picks one off.
A dive with area damage (Kael'thas Living Bomb, Gazlowe Grav-O-Bomb, Li-Ming) wipes grouped Vikings and they are already a man down in the fight.
Global heroes with wave clear (Dehaka, Falstad) can double soak and still join fights, which removes their experience advantage.
Heroes that hit structures hard (Zagara, Greymane) can win a siege race against their lane pressure without needing to fight.

wants_from_team: a traditional comp with a main tank, a sustain healer (Malfurion) and a sustained damage dealer
heroes with strong lane presence that can push as four
a long range caster to stall objectives while the Vikings are split
team that knows when the Vikings are away
gives_team: large experience and level lead
three lane pressure and fort damage
camp control with Viking Bribery
interrupt for channeled objectives
weaknesses: weak early game in lane
tiny health pools, easy to pick off
weak on two lane maps

team plays a man down in fights

kit.strength: Chain Lightning, Feral Spirit and Windfury give lane pressure and camp clear.
kit.weak: Lacks burst early and has to be near targets.

attack.note: Melee basic attacks boosted by Windfury (three fast hits, Tempest Fury adds three more), Maelstrom Weapon, Elemental Assault and Alpha Wolf. Chain Lightning gives ranged ability damage, but he is not a ranged damage dealer.

poke.note: Chain Lightning is a targeted spell with 4 bounces (Rolling Thunder), 7 second cooldown and a Thunderstorm slow and damage stack. It cannot be dodged but does limited damage and costs mana. This is the recommended build when the enemy has weak healing.

damage.note: Windfury attacks, Feral Spirit root and Sundering stun produce a short burst on one target. Rolling Thunder, Ancestral Wrath and Alpha Wolf add percent health damage. Frostwolf Resilience heals him as he deals ability damage. Measured damage 2661 per minute is well above the 2060 median with strong takedown numbers (9.6 per game).

cc.note: Feral Spirit roots for 1 second (1.5 with Alpha Wolf) and hits in a line. Sundering stuns for 1 second and shoves. Earthquake slows by 50 percent over three pulses. Measured 40 seconds of enemy CC per game, the highest of this set.

good_into.why: Feral Spirit roots and Sundering stuns, Windfury and Wind Rush close the gap. Earthquake slows 50 percent in an area so targets cannot leave.

Alpha Wolf (3 percent max health), Rolling Thunder (3 percent) and Ancestral Wrath (15 percent over 3 seconds) are percent damage and the guide recommends the Feral Spirit build against more than two high health heroes such as Azmodan.
The Chain Lightning build pokes with 4 bounce lightning and Thunderstorm before the fight. With no healer or a low sustain one the chip does not come back.
Sundering splits the enemy team and Feral Spirit with Windfury and Tempest Fury bursts a rooted target. Wind Rush closes onto a flank.

bad_into.why: Low mobility. The guide names Lunara style kiters, only Windfury (30 percent speed for 4 seconds) and Wind Rush on a 90 second cooldown close the gap.
Blinds ruin Windfury and Tempest Fury, and stun plus burst (Kael'thas) kills him before his abilities land. Spirit Shield only covers one ability.
He has no wave clear to relieve pressure and fights only in team fights. Frostwolf Resilience needs ability hits to heal.
Heroes who can kite his Feral Spirit and stay out of melee reach deny the combo. Chain Lightning is his only answer at range.

wants_from_team: A real offlaner or a team that does not need his wave clear
Allied area damage that benefits from his Earthquake slow (Jaina, Diablo, Fenix)
A healer or tank so he can engage with Sundering safely
A 4 man team that fights together, not split lanes
gives_team: Hard engage and interrupt with Sundering
Roots, slows and zone with Earthquake
Burst on a priority target
Shields for the team with Earthen Shields

Low mobility

Needs team to play 4 man
profile.owner_notes: A bruiser or melee assassin with decent sustain and damage. Slower than Sonya at clearing waves and taking or defending camps.

kit.strength: Blink and Recall make her very hard to kill.
kit.weak: Low damage and range and demands high skill.

attack.note: Moves while attacking, 10 round magazine, lifesteal on hits. Almost all her output is basic attacks plus Melee and Pulse Bomb. Attack range is short for a ranged hero, so she must stay near targets.

poke.note: She has no real poke tool. Her basic attacks work only up close, and her main damage comes when she dives in. Pulse Bomb is short range and not a harass tool.

damage.note: A hit and run assassin: a stream of fast autos, Melee for burst and a Pulse Bomb that sticks to a target. Single target focus on squishy heroes. Healing helps against her only when it can keep up with a diver, and Melee plus Pulse Bomb are burst. Ricochet adds some spread damage.

good_into.why: Blink, Melee and a stuck Pulse Bomb can delete a low health ranged hero or healer in a couple of seconds; Icy Veins calls her very good against fragile heroes who lack mobility.
Targets that cannot move away are chased down by Blink and Recall, and cannot sidestep Pulse Bomb.
Single target healers struggle to keep up when she bursts a target with Melee and a bomb, and she can also lifesteal back.
She kites melee heroes with Blink and attack while moving, and Jumper shields and charges keep her slippery.
Her mobility and Recall let her catch isolated heroes who are caught away from the team.

bad_into.why: Stuns, silences, polymorphs and knockbacks stop Blink and Melee combos and can prevent Recall, which is her only cleanse.
Heroes with long range basic attacks (Raynor, Sgt. Hammer per the guide) punish her short range and low health.
Area healing and spread damage let a team soak her chip damage and wait out Recall.
She does not deal much against armored tanks and cannot get past a frontline into a backline protected by CC.
She has no reveal for basic abilities, so stealthed assassins escape her chase, though Pulse Bomb can reveal on hit.

wants_from_team: Reliable wave clear so she can focus on heroes
A tank with hard CC to catch targets
A healer who can heal at range (Malfurion style)
Peel because she is fragile when caught
gives_team: Backline pickoffs and threat on enemy squishies
Constant pressure on enemy frontline from the edge of fights
Finishing power on fleeing low health heroes
Map rotations that punish split enemies

kit.strength: Minigun and Commandeer Odin give strong sustained damage.

attack.note: Minigun gives an attack speed of 4 per second and the active adds percent max health damage, but he cannot stutter step and has low range for the class. Overkill is a channeled ability that does most of his moving damage.

poke.note: Quarterback with Titan Grenade gives Frag Grenade poke and Spray n Pray extends Overkill, but base range is short and a knockback grenade is a cooldown, not constant poke.

damage.note: Minigun adds 2.5 percent of max health per hit for 3 seconds and Sizzlin Attacks and Titan Grenade stack more percent effects, so he melts tanks and high health heroes through healing. Overkill and Minigun are interruptible by stuns, silences and blinds, which is his main way of being stopped.

Against low health targets Minigun percent damage is worth less and The Bigger They Are stops affecting targets under 30 percent.

kit.strength: Sanctification and Judgment protect allies and El'druin's Might gives global reach.
kit.weak: Does not start fights alone and loses value away from allies.

attack.note: Ardent Restoration, Purge Evil, Divine Vigor, Horadric Reforging and Seal of El'druin all run through basic attacks, and the recommended build is called Basic Attacks Build.

poke.note: El'druin's Might (110) and Smite (150, 6 second cooldown) are thrown at an area. With Sword of Justice he can throw, hit and teleport back, which gives poke with some risk.

damage.note: Burning Halo gives constant area damage (12 per second, more after a teleport) and Smite is a decent burst. 1836 damage per minute is high for a tank. Ardent Restoration and Divine Vigor heal from damage dealt, so he is helped by dealing damage and hurt by healing reduction.

good_into.why: Sanctification makes the whole team Invulnerable for 3 seconds (4 with Holy Arena), so a chain of stuns, roots and silences does nothing. Judgment is Unstoppable while he charges.
Sanctification and Righteousness (350 shield, 80 percent to allies with Justice for All) answer a dive. Archangel's Wrath cuts the damage of nearby enemies by 50 percent if he dies.
Judgment (150 damage, 1.5 second stun, knocks nearby enemies away) with Angel of Justice lets him land on a backline hero with a partner like Illidan or Falstad.

Holy Ground and Sanctification are strong in static fights but he has 2794 siege per minute and no global presence, so he does not answer a team that avoids the fight.

kit.strength: Sentinel, Lunar Flare and Shadowstalk add poke and pick damage while healing.
kit.weak: Less healing than dedicated healers and fragile.

attack.note: Basic attacks drive her healing and her kit: every hit cuts Light of Elune cooldown by 1.5 seconds, Hunter's Mark heals her, Elune's Chosen turns attacks into healing and Ranger's Mark cuts Lunar Flare cooldown. Moonlit Arrows and Darnassian Archery add to that.

poke.note: Sentinel is a long line skillshot for 120 that reveals, Lunar Flare is a delayed stun skillshot for 150, Starfall adds area damage. Measured hero damage 1771 per minute is the highest of this group.

damage.note: Hunter's Mark lowers armor by 15 and amplifies focus fire. Empower adds percent health damage. She adds damage to her team more than she deals it herself.

healing.note: Light of Elune is 270 on a 2 charge, 16 second recharge that attacks and Starfall cut down. Hunter's Mark takes 15 Armor off a tank and boosts all damage on them, Trueshot Aura adds 40 percent attack damage, and Mark of Mending heals the team while attacking the marked tank.
Lunar Flare is a delayed skillshot, so slow targets are stunned reliably and Celestial Wrath slows them more.

kit.strength: Holy Light, Hammer of Justice and Divine Shield give big heals, a stun and protection.
kit.weak: Limited mobility and vulnerable to dive.

attack.note: Basic attacks fuel Hammer of the Lightbringer, Blessed Champion, Holy Fire and Tyr's Deliverance but the guide treats them as an extra, not a core.

poke.note: Holy Radiance deals 177 damage in a line alongside the heal, and Holy Shock adds 145 with the right talent. This is incidental. Measured hero damage 868 per minute.

damage.note: Hammer of Justice is a 109 damage targeted stun, so his damage is about crowd control, not output.

healing.note: Holy Light is a 362 instant heal at 80 Mana and Devotion gives 25 Armor on every basic ability heal, with Eternal Vanguard giving about 6 free Flash of Light heals after death and Redemption reviving him. Hammer plus Well Met slow and damage reduction and Divine Storm area stun lock melee Heroes, and Hammer of the Lightbringer punishes those who get close.
Holy Radiance and Holy Fire reveal stealthed Heroes, which gives Hammer of Justice a target.

attack.note: Almost all damage is Sinister Strike, Ambush, Garrote and Eviscerate. Autos matter only with Slice and Dice, Hemorrhage and Rupture.

Cheap Shot stuns and blinds basic attack reliant assassins and Smoke Bomb gives 60 percent damage reduction against them.

Shield Wall makes Parry full invulnerability against burst and Demoralizing Shout reduces incoming damage, though this costs his damage.

kit.weak: Low defense and reliant on cooldowns.

damage.note: Her damage is small tick damage that enemy healing absorbs, and her Zeal healing is cut by healing reduction. Subjugation (minus 50 percent damage on Inquisition target) matters more than her raw damage.

healing.note: Zeal returns 100 percent of damage she deals to Heroes as healing to every ally with Zeal, so output scales with damage and with the number of Zealed allies. Out of combat healing is weak without Martyrdom, and healing reduction (Ana, Deckard Cain Sapphire) cuts it hard.

good_into.why: She heals off damage to any Hero, so a durable frontline that stays in the fight gives Zeal steady conversion. Shared Punishment and Purge the Wicked cut their Armor.
Melee Heroes stay in range of Inquisition and Searing Lash and pay for it with Subjugation halving their damage, and Scarlet Aegis Armor reduces their autos.
Scarlet Aegis heals the whole team and gives 40 Armor, Intercession and Scarlet Crusade free allies from stuns, and Subjugation shrinks the diver's damage.
Inquisition slow and Divine Reckoning with Judgment Day pull keep low mobility Heroes in the damage zone, which feeds Zeal.

Long fights burn her Mana through Desperation stacks and poke at range lets the enemy hit her team while she cannot trade.

poke.note: Void Volley is a delayed 6 orb barrage, Shadow Mark is a very slow projectile with a small center, and Dark Heart Ritual pulses an area. All telegraphed and dodgeable by mobile heroes, but strong against slow or controlled targets.

damage.note: A mage like assassin that mixes burst (Marked target plus Dark Heart detonation, Void Volley, Void Eruption explosion up to 700) with pulsing zone damage. Toxic Mark adds 1 percent max health a second and an armor shred. The burst needs setup, so healers can undo the spread pulses, but not a clean burst combo.

good_into.why: Her own team's CC gives her a window to land Shadow Mark, and Dark Heart's Protection can silence an enemy engage in a choke.
Slow telegraphed skillshots and Void Eruption land fully on targets that cannot step away.
Pull of the Dark Heart, Fractured Reality fire trails and Void Eruption's blind punish melee heroes that must walk through her zone.
Anchored Core Dark Heart Ritual repeatedly interrupts 5 and 6 second channels at tributes, seeds and altars.
Physical basic attacks, armor shred from Toxic Mark and percent max health damage cut through armor and large health pools.

Shadow Mark reveals only a target it hits, so stealth heroes can approach while she has no answer.
Dark Heart pulses and Toxic Mark ticks are spread damage that sustained healing can offset.

A tank who peels when she is hunted

kit.strength: Raise Skeleton, Bone Armor and Cursed Strikes give lane control and sustained damage.
kit.weak: Fragile when skeletons are dead and weak to CC.

attack.note: Cursed Strikes makes every basic attack cleave and cut enemy attack speed 40 percent for 4 seconds (5 attacks). Harvest Vitality, Rapid Harvest and Grim Scythe all build on autos. Spectral Scythe returns to him after a delay and is a skillshot, not a ranged dealer role.

poke.note: Spectral Scythe (190, 1 second delay) and Echoes of Death hit a line and can be dodged. Bone Spear is a line poke with a 12 second cooldown. Poison Nova is a 10 second dot that melee heroes cannot dodge but ranged heroes can.

damage.note: Skeletal Warriors, Cursed Strikes cleave and Poison Nova (630 over 10 seconds) are spread chip damage. A strong AoE healer undoes Poison Nova, while Mortal Wound cuts healing by 75 percent after a scythe hit. Measured siege damage 8011 per minute is far above the median 4430, and hero damage 2002 is near the median.

cc.note: Bone Prison has a 2 second delay and roots for 1.75 seconds (2 with Amplify Damage). Skeletal Mages and Decrepify slow 30 percent. Cursed Strikes is attack speed reduction, not movement. Measured CC on enemies 29.6 seconds per game.

good_into.why: Cursed Strikes cleaves and slows attack speed 40 percent, Poison Nova hits melee heroes that cannot dodge it, and Weaken cuts their damage 35 percent. The guide says he excels against melee compositions.
Poison Nova over 10 seconds is hard for Lt. Morales or Uther to undo across a team, and the guide names this. Mortal Wound adds 75 percent healing reduction.
Wave clear plus Raise Skeleton make minion waves pile onto towers while he rotates, so he wins lanes and siege when the enemy does not answer.
Cleave and AoE abilities clear summons and pets cheaply and his own skeletons win exchanges against them.

Mobile burst heroes (Jaina, Sgt. Hammer, Zeratul) follow up crowd control before Bone Armor lasts. Low early game and no escape.
Poke gets full value because he has no way to engage and Cursed Strikes does nothing against distance.

kit.strength: Righteous Hammer and Ardent Defender give sustain and Vindication supports allies.
kit.weak: Falls off against sustained CC.
