kit.strength: Creep Tumors, Hunter Killer and Nydus Network give elite wave clear and map pressure.
kit.weak: Low team fight impact and fragile.

attack.note: Base range is 6.6 and Jagged Barbs adds 1.1 on creep. Her summons (Hunter Killer, Infested Drop roaches) and creep buffs matter more than her own autos, but autos are the harass tool and reduce cooldowns with Nydus Network.

poke.note: Baneling Barrage has slow shots that are easy to avoid when spammed, and Infested Drop has a delay. Her real poke is Hunter Killer, which locks onto a target and cannot be dodged, plus long range basic attacks on creep.

damage.note: A siege and summon based damage dealer: Hunter Killer hydralisks, roaches and banelings deal damage over time at long range. The damage is spread across many small sources, which sustained healing can offset, except Corrosive Saliva which adds percent max health. Devouring Maw is a unique removal for 4 seconds that cannot be countered by unstoppable.

good_into.why: Infest, Mutalisk, Nydus Network and Creep Tumor let her push and rotate; measured siege is 5365 per minute and merc camps 3.4 a game.
Corrosive Saliva adds 1.5 percent max health damage through Hunter Killer and roaches, and Pack Instinct boosts damage on the target.
Hunter Killer, Banelings, Infest and Mutalisk tear down forts and keeps, which is her best known strength.
Devouring Maw removes enemy heroes for 4 seconds even if Unstoppable, and allies can chain CC when they come out.
Hunter Killer on creep and Viscous Acid slow let her kite, and Medusa Blades handles minion flood.

bad_into.why: Heroes like Falstad and Dehaka limit her split pushing, per Icy Veins.
High mobility assassins such as Illidan outsustain and stick to her even on creep, and she has no mobility.
Her damage comes from many small hits and summons that healers can undo, which weakens lane control and poke.
Baneling and Drop shots are slow and telegraphed, so mobile heroes avoid them and then dive her.
A team that catches her away from allies kills her before Spell Shield or Nydus Network help.

wants_from_team: One or two tanks to hold the frontline
CC chains to combo with Devouring Maw
Wave presence from teammates while she split pushes
Vision and map awareness for ganks
gives_team: Elite wave clear and camp clear to free the team
Siege and structure pressure
Map wide vision from Creep Tumor
Devouring Maw as team fight setup
weaknesses: No mobility off creep
Mana hungry
Low burst
Hunter Killer and Maw are easy to disrupt with CC and ganks

kit.strength: Personal Barrier, Shield Ally and Graviton Surge give strong team protection.
kit.weak: Poor wave clear and weak against kiting.

attack.note: Her beam attack hits every enemy in a line and Feel the Heat gives 50 percent more damage to enemies in melee range, so her damage is mostly autos plus Particle Grenade. Short range, not a long range attacker.

poke.note: Particle Grenade has 4 charges, 80 damage and is better at high Energy. Pinpoint Accuracy adds slow at the center. It is real poke with a grenade arc that can be walked out of.

damage.note: Energy is 2 percent more damage per point, up to 100 percent. Measured hero damage 2354 per minute is above the league median, so she deals real damage, but it is built from beams and grenades that healing and constant damage keep her from building. Her damage depends on absorbing damage, so a team with little damage to absorb leaves her weak.

healing.note: Not a healer for the draft. Shield Ally is 420 for 3 seconds on a 12 second cooldown (Gain Train adds a second ally, Cleansing Shield removes crowd control). It stops a burst but expires quickly, so the guide lists weakness to sustained damage. No mana cost.

good_into.why: Personal Barrier (560) and Shield Ally (420) absorb a burst combo, and the absorbed damage becomes Energy. The guide says she shines against Jaina style burst and aggressive assassins such as Kerrigan.
Feel the Heat deals 50 percent more to enemies in melee range, Expulsion Zone knocks them back and Defensive Shielding blocks 2 hits. Melee heroes have to stand inside her beam.
The guide says Feel the Heat is best against low mobility, low range heroes, and Graviton Surge or Expulsion Zone in a choke point traps them.
Unstoppable Competitor makes her Unstoppable with Personal Barrier and Cleansing Shield removes crowd control from an ally, so she can keep a carry free.

bad_into.why: Lunara and similar heroes walk away from a short range, no mobility hero. Her Energy decays by 3 per second when she cannot absorb damage.
Shields last 3 seconds and constant chip damage (Raynor, Chromie) outlasts them, and the damage she absorbs is only Energy if it comes in bursts. Varian Shattering Throw breaks them.
She has no mobility and cannot catch a Genji or Tracer. The guide says blinds are quite effective against her because much of her damage is basic attacks.
Displacement such as Wrecking Ball and skillshots (Maiev) hit her because she has no escape, and her own crowd control is only two heroics.

wants_from_team: a marksman or burst hero that benefits from her shields (Valla, a sustain healer like Malfurion)
a main tank, a solid offlaner and a healer, because she covers none of these
an offlaner who can double soak on three lane maps
choke points around objectives for her heroics
gives_team: damage shields on demand
movement speed with Speed Barrier
area denial and cleanse
a costless ranged damage source
weaknesses: no mobility
shields are short and break against constant damage
weak wave clear
weak to blind and displacement
depends on incoming damage for Energy

kit.strength: Blink and Permanent Cloak give top mobility and map presence, Void Prison wins picks.
kit.weak: Fragile and punished by detection and misses.

attack.note: Might of the Nerazim, Master Warp-Blade, Mending Strikes and Psionic Strength all reward weaving autos between abilities. Singularity Spike is his only ranged ability and is usually cast from melee.

poke.note: Singularity Spike can be fired from range but the guide says to avoid using it as poke because it is easy to heal off and a long cooldown.

damage.note: Cleave, Singularity Spike with a slow and weaved autos burst a squishy target in a couple of seconds, and Twilight Falls doubles the rotation. Mending Strikes lets him out sustain weak healers in 1v1. Burst gets through healing, but a fully healed and shielded target (Medivh, Uther, Divine Shield) survives.

good_into.why: Permanent Cloak, Blink and Vorpal Blade reach the backline unseen and Cleave plus Singularity Spike plus Might of the Nerazim kill it fast.
Stealth flanks bypass the front line, and Void Prison can split the enemy team in half so allies fight only the backline.
Mending Strikes and Shadow Mending beat weak healers in a duel and burst kills before an Uther or Morales heal lands.
Move Unseen gives fast stealth rotations and ganks on lone heroes, and Void Prison can freeze a camp or a structure.

bad_into.why: Targeted CC (Polymorph, Twilight Dream, Warlord's Challenge) hits him in the Wormhole window or after he commits, and he has low health.
Revealing abilities such as Eye of Kilrogg or area damage strip his main strength and leave a fragile hero exposed.
He is easy to kill once revealed and relies on cooldown timing for Blink, so he cannot trade with a dive comp.
Heroes who can react to Blink with their own gap closer leave him with no reliable follow up if Vorpal Blade fails.

wants_from_team: Allies who follow his dives
Sustained AoE damage dealers (Sylvanas, Gul'dan)
Combo partners for Void Prison (Diablo, Jaina)
Early game strength since he is weak early
gives_team: Backline assassination and pickoffs
Void Prison setup for team combos or a split
Stealth ganks and map pressure
Strong mobility with several blinks
weaknesses: Vulnerable to targeted crowd control and reveals
Low base health for a melee assassin
Weak early game, depends on Level 16 talents
High skill floor

kit.strength: Berserker, Twin Cleave and Taz'dingo provide heavy sustained damage.
kit.weak: Low mobility and punished by CC.

attack.note: Berserker boosts attack speed as health drops and the active adds 25 percent attack damage. You Want Axe? grows range and damage. Basic attacks are the core damage with Grievous Throw marks, though the Twin Cleave build shifts weight onto abilities.

poke.note: Twin Cleave is an area arc with a slow that is tricky to land, Grievous Throw is a simple line. Range grows with You Want Axe? and Headhunter, but there is no safe constant poke.

damage.note: A high single target basic attack carry with a burst option: Grievous Throw marks add 50 percent damage, Guillotine scales as his health drops. Berserker makes him stronger while hurt, so he can trade through some healing. The Twin Cleave build adds area poke and burst on squishies.

good_into.why: Grievous Throw with Vicious Assault and No Mercy ignores armor and adds percent max health; the guide names Garrosh and Uther as targets.
Twin Cleave plus Guillotine with Recklessness can delete ranged assassins and healers in one combo.
Taz'dingo and Berserker let him trade through single target healing, and Amani Resilience heals him back.
Twin Cleave slows and Ensnare roots, and Eye of Zul'jin move speed lets him kite.
Heavy healing teams let him use Berserker safely and keep attacking, with a healer to manage his health drain.

bad_into.why: Stuns and silences before Taz'dingo kill him and he has only Voodoo Shuffle for roots and slows.
He has no gap closer or escape and low health, and dives kill him before Regeneration helps.
A stealth or blind hero shuts down a basic attack carry; Blinding Wind is cited by the guide as a severe counter.
Berserker lowers his health on purpose, so a burst team punishes low health states.
Mobile ranged heroes can avoid Twin Cleave and out trade his medium range basic attacks.

wants_from_team: A strong frontline to peel for him
A healer to manage Berserker health drain
Allied CC to land Twin Cleave and Guillotine
Shields or move speed buffs from the healer (Uther, Tyrael, Whitemane style)
gives_team: High single target basic attack damage
Burst on squishies with Twin Cleave and Guillotine
A slow from Twin Cleave for pickoffs
Unkillable Taz'dingo window for team fights
weaknesses: No gap closer and very susceptible to ganks
Overusing Berserker leaves low health
Weak when blinded or crowd controlled
High skill floor for Twin Cleave

Alterac Pass.name: Alterac Pass
Alterac Pass.notes: - Hunter's best Sylvanas map (9-5). CCS beat us here with 15 deaths. Anchor, camp clearers, objective poke, self sustain.

Battlefield of Eternity.name: Battlefield of Eternity
Battlefield of Eternity.notes: - Early game and camps. We beat Cosmos here in 13 minutes on Oct 6 with Johanna, Brightwing, Li-Ming, Tychus and Blaze. Chen and Sylvanas are S tier.

Dragon Shire.name: Dragon Shire
Dragon Shire.notes: - Needs sustain and a durable shrine holder. CCS beat us here in 26 minutes with 18 of our deaths. Brightwing or Rehgar, Leoric for the shrine, Hanzo is their pick to ban.

Garden of Terror.name: Garden of Terror
Garden of Terror.notes:
- Camp clearers, a double bruiser, Rehgar. Two or fewer ranged heroes (4-1, against 0-3 with three or more).
- We are 3-1 here, all with Rehgar. The loss was to Qhira, Anub'arak, Li-Ming, Tyrande and Ragnaros. Do not leave the tank alone in the front.

Infernal Shrines.name: Infernal Shrines
Infernal Shrines.notes: - CCS is 2-1 and has won both of its own picks here. Ban it. If it comes up: double healer and high wave clear. Three or more ranged heroes is 7-3 on this map.

Sky Temple.name: Sky Temple
Sky Temple.notes:
- Our best map against CCS (we won, they lost on their own pick). Camp clearers, gankers, split push. Sylvanas is 7-4 here in Storm League.
- Chen is S tier here. Ban Ragnaros if CCS shows it.

Tomb of the Spider Queen.name: Tomb of the Spider Queen
Tomb of the Spider Queen.notes:
- Three or more ranged heroes (7-3) and two high clear heroes, one of them ranged. Two or fewer ranged is 2-6.
- Hunter on Chromie or Sylvanas, chelsi on Tassadar, Gul'dan or Tychus. Do not repeat the Oct 6 draft (Sylvanas, Thrall, Leoric, Rehgar, Tyrael, one ranged hero).
- Hunter's Storm League record here is his worst (31-39).

Towers of Doom.name: Towers of Doom
Towers of Doom.notes: - CCS is 4-1 here. We are 0-1. Ban it. If it comes up: gankers, camp clearers, an offlaner who can double soak.

Volskaya Foundry.name: Volskaya Foundry
Volskaya Foundry.notes: - Late game, siege damage and sustain. Hunter's weaker map in Storm League (48%), so Sylvanas, Valla or Orphea and not Hanzo or Li-Ming. We beat CCS here in 18 minutes with two deaths.

Can't Counterpick Stupid.name: Can't Counterpick Stupid
Can't Counterpick Stupid.notes:
## How they win and lose
- Deaths decide it. All four of our losses to them had 15 to 18 of our deaths. When CCS loses, every one of their players dies about twice as often (Valkamer 1.6 to 3.2, WitsEnd 1.2 to 3.2, UnicycleYay 1.6 to 3.2, ultear 1.7 to 3.5).
- Kill ultear (Gold 3) first and make WitsEnd leave Lunara. Do not chase kills on side lanes where ShadowDroid and WitsEnd can catch us.
- ShadowDroid is the clear and camp engine (5.7k minion damage a minute). Deny him Gazlowe.

## Healer pattern
- CCS is 4-6 against teams with Brightwing or Anduin and 12-1 against every other healer (Anomaly beat them once on Oct 14 without either). We are 2-1 with Brightwing against them and 0-3 with Rehgar or Stukov. Lock Brightwing early. It has never been banned against us.

## Qhira (UnicycleYay)
- He is 2-3 on Qhira with 4.0 deaths a game and 12-3 on everything else (Sylvanas, Hanzo, Tychus, Valla, Garrosh, Diablo). Do not spend a round one ban on her. The one time we did, he took Sylvanas and went 7/0/9.
- If she is in the draft, answer with a stun tank, Brightwing, a ranged poker, and kill her in the fights. Cosmos beat her three times that way.

## Draft timing
- They ban Junkrat and Chromie in round one (slots 1 to 4) and Thrall and Tychus in round two (slot 10 or 11). A hero already picked cannot be banned. Lock Thrall or Tychus by slot 9 (first pick) or slot 7 (second pick).
- They have never banned Sylvanas or Brightwing against us.
- Johanna is their favorite first pick (Valkamer 6-1) and counters Tychus and Brightwing. We ban it.

## Coin toss
- They are 12-2 with first pick and 3-4 when they pick the map. When they have first pick against us we are 0-2. Take first pick.

## Their Garden of Terror comp
- Qhira, Anub'arak, Li-Ming, Tyrande and Ragnaros beat us on fights (5.0k against 3.5k fight damage a minute) and experience (3.33k against 2.69k). Ban Ragnaros. Chen and Stukov answer Ragnaros, Leoric or Varian answer Anub'arak.

damage_delivery.question: How does the hero actually produce damage?

values.auto_attacker: most damage is basic attacks (Valla, Tychus, Raynor, Greymane)
values.ability_caster: most damage is abilities, autos are filler (Li-Ming, Jaina, Kael'thas)
values.hybrid: autos and abilities both carry the damage (Sylvanas, Cassia, Falstad)
values.summoner: pets, turrets or minions do the work (Azmodan, Zagara, Probius, Kel'Thuzad, Gazlowe)
values.zone_trap: damage comes from areas and traps the enemy walks into (Junkrat, Abathur nests)
values.melee_brawler: close range autos and abilities in a fight (Illidan, Sonya, Zeratul)
values.channel: damage is a channelled or charged ability that is easy to interrupt
values.utility_minimal: its damage is not why it is picked

damage_delivery.draft_use: Tells whether a comp has the right MIX of damage sources and what interrupts it.

damage_timing.question: When in a fight does the damage arrive?

values.burst_window: big damage in a short window, then waits on cooldowns
values.sustained_dps: steady damage as long as it stays alive and in range
values.chip_poke: small, repeated damage from range that wears targets down
values.execute_finisher: strongest on low health or marked targets
values.ramp_up: weak at first, scales through a fight or the game

damage_timing.draft_use: Burst beats healing and shields, chip is beaten by healing, so this pairs with the healer and tank lenses.

damage_reach.question: From how far can it deal its damage in a fight?

values.point_blank: must be on top of the target
values.short: short range, a few hero lengths
values.long: outranges most heroes and many abilities

damage_reach.draft_use: Range wars: who can hit whom without being hit, and what a melee front line can reach.

target_style.question: What does the damage hit?

values.percent_health: percent of max health damage that tanks feel
values.structure_focus: built to hit forts, towers and cores
values.minion_focus: wave clear first, hero damage second

target_style.draft_use: Percent damage and single target answer tanks, aoe answers clumped and squishy teams.

damage_reliability.question: What must go right for the damage to land?

values.guaranteed: point and click or auto attacks that always hit once in range
values.skillshot: must aim abilities, can be dodged
values.setup_needed: needs a partner CC, a stun or a stack first
values.stack_or_quest: depends on stacks or a quest that takes time or has to be protected
values.positioning: needs a flank, a safe angle or a specific stance
values.interruptible_channel: damage comes from a channel any CC cancels
values.blockable: blocked by minions, summons or terrain
values.telegraphed_delay: a visible delay the target can leave

damage_reliability.draft_use: Skillshot damage is weak into mobile heroes, setup damage needs partners with CC.

frontline_style.question: What kind of front line is this hero (tanks and bruisers)?

values.initiator: starts fights with a big engage
values.anchor_peeler: holds position and protects the backline
values.disruptor: breaks up the enemy team, pulls or knocks back
values.brawler_sustain: wins long fights by outlasting, lifesteal or self heals
values.dive_bruiser: jumps on the backline and fights there
values.zone_controller: denies space with walls, fields and slows
values.not_frontline: does not take the front line
values.catcher: a tank built to catch targets and get kills, not only to hold the line (Diablo, Garrosh)

frontline_style.draft_use: A comp usually needs one hero that initiates and one that protects; two initiators with no peel is a coin flip.

durability_source.question: How does it stay alive?

values.relies_on_healer: needs a healer to stay in the fight
values.second_body_or_pool: a second health pool or body (D.Va, Cho and Gall)

durability_source.draft_use: Heroes that rely on a healer bring more value into low pressure fights and less into dive.

lane_role.question: Where does it want to play before the fights?

values.solo_laner: can take a lane alone and hold or push it
values.split_pusher: wins by pushing a lane alone and pulling attention
values.rotator: moves between lanes and fights, does not hold a lane
values.soak_and_group: groups with the team and soaks with it
values.camp_taker: takes mercenary camps to speed rotations
values.no_lane: does not want a lane at all
values.lane_bully: wins its lane early and uses it
values.double_soaker: goes to a lane with a partner to double soak (Samuro, Malthael)

lane_role.draft_use: A draft needs a lane plan: one solo laner and who rotates.

kill_pattern.question: How does it get kills?

values.backline_dive: jumps over the front line to the backline
values.flank_pick: comes from the side or behind to pick off a hero
values.stealth_ambush: stealth or untargetable setup then burst
values.burst_snipe: a long range burst on a target
values.cc_chain: catches with CC and others finish
values.attrition: wins by chip damage and positional squeezing
values.pull_pick: a single pull picks a target (Stitches, Diablo)

kill_pattern.draft_use: Pick comps want several different kill patterns; dive comps want the CC chain to hold the backline.

escape.question: Can it get out after it commits or is caught?

values.partial: one escape on a cooldown or conditional
values.none: no escape, a catch is a death

escape.draft_use: Heroes with no escape are the targets of dive and stun comps, and are kept alive by peel.

setup_reliance.question: Does it start things or finish things?

values.self_starter: can create its own kill opportunities
values.needs_cc_partner: needs another hero CC or engage to get value
values.needs_peel: needs to be protected to deal damage
values.cleanup: cleans up after a fight started by others
values.enabler: its job is to make others work (Medivh, Lucio, Abathur)

setup_reliance.draft_use: Counts of needs_cc_partner heroes must be matched by CC providers on the comp.

healer_class.question: What kind of healer or support is this?

values.burst_single: big heals on one target (Uther, Ana, Anduin)
values.sustain_single: steady healing on one or two targets (Malfurion, Deckard, Li Li)
values.aoe_sustain: heals many people through chip damage (Brightwing, Lucio, Stukov, Auriel)
values.hit_and_run: weak heals, strong mobility or utility
values.utility_support: buffs, speed, vision or macro tools more than healing
values.damage_fueled: heals scale with damage it or an ally deals (Auriel, Tyrande, Whitemane, Kharazim)

healer_class.draft_use: Match healers to comps: poke teams want sustain, dive teams want burst heals, a shield support makes a squishy comp playable.

healer_safety.question: How exposed is the healer?

values.safe: heals from range or has escapes
values.conditional: safe when positioned well or peeled
values.exposed: must be in danger to heal

healer_safety.draft_use: An exposed healer into dive is a trade you lose.

utility_tool.question: What non damage tool does it bring?

values.speed_buff: speed aura or buff to the team

utility_tool.draft_use: Utility explains why a hero is picked beyond damage and healing.

cc_profile.question: How much CC and what kind?

values.chain_hard: two or more reliable hard CC tools that chain
values.single_hard: one reliable hard CC (a stun or silence)
values.talent_dependent: CC only if a talent is taken
values.knockback_pull: knockbacks and pulls only (Raynor, Alarak, Kerrigan, Lt. Morales)

cc_profile.draft_use: Comps need several hard CC tools to hold targets for burst; too little means damage dealers cannot land setup combos.

cc_delivery.question: How hard is the CC to land?

values.skillshot: must be aimed, can be dodged

cc_delivery.draft_use: Skillshot CC into mobile heroes is unreliable; point and click chains beat mobile comps.

anti_cc.question: How does it deal with enemy CC?

values.shield_or_bubble: block or shield that protects it
values.mobility_through: dash or leap out of CC
values.ally_only_denial: denies CC only on allies (Anduin, Li Li)

anti_cc.draft_use: Heavy CC comps are blanked by cleanse and unstoppable tools, so a team needs at least one answer.

wave_clear_style.question: How does it clear lanes?

values.aoe_burst: one or two abilities clear a wave fast
values.summons_or_zone: pets, turrets or zones clear while it does other things

wave_clear_style.draft_use: Maps with waves and objectives need at least one burst or summon clearer; zero is a macro loss.

camp_play.question: Can it take mercenary camps well?

values.ok: can take camps with some time

camp_play.draft_use: Camp control sets the tempo for objective timings.

objective_role.question: What does it do at objectives?

values.zone_hold: holds ground at the objective with CC and zone
values.global_presence: impacts both objective and lanes from far away
values.siege_pressure: pressures forts and keeps the enemy honest between objectives

objective_role.draft_use: Different maps reward different objective roles.

split_potential.question: How well can it split push or draw attention in a lane?

values.strong: a one hero lane that must be answered
values.some: can split briefly or with a talent

split_potential.draft_use: A split comp needs one hero strong at it and the rest able to fight 4 on 5 or hold.

map_mobility.question: How fast can it move around the map and into a fight?
map_mobility.draft_use: Mobility decides who wins rotations; low mobility comps lose double objectives.

vision_stealth.question: What does it do for vision and information?

power_curve.question: When is it strongest?

values.early_dominant: early lane and early fight power, loses value late
values.late_scaler: weak early, dominates at level 16 to 20
values.stack_dependent: power depends on a quest or stacks

power_curve.draft_use: Early comps want fights before level 10, late scalers want long games; a draft with both is confused.

snowball.question: How does it react to leads and deficits?

values.snowballer: gets much stronger from kills or leads
values.comeback: has a way to come back (global ult, long range siege, mobility)

snowball.draft_use: Snowball comps punish slow starts; comeback tools are insurance.

ultimate_role.question: What is its heroic or ultimate for?

values.teamfight_swing: swings a fight when it lands
values.low_impact: weak heroic, the hero is picked for its basic kit

ultimate_role.draft_use: A comp needs a fight swinger, and the opposing comp ults should be answered.

execution_demand.question: How hard is it to play well?
execution_demand.draft_use: A comfort pick for the player usually beats a theoretically better pick that is hard.

team_needs.question: What does it need from the team to function?

values.front_line: a front line to stand behind
values.wave_clear: someone else clears waves while it fights
values.burst_follow_up: burst damage right after its CC (Anub'arak, Garrosh, Malthael's partners)

team_needs.draft_use: Counting needs across the five heroes shows whether the comp ask exceeds what it provides.

team_gives.question: What does it give its teammates?

values.burst_follow_up: burst damage after a team CC

team_gives.draft_use: The comp checker adds gives against needs.

vulnerable_to.question: What does it lose to?

values.dive: enemy dives and assassins reaching it
values.hard_cc: stuns, roots and silences while exposed
values.sustain_heals: enemy healing that blunts its damage
values.stealth: stealth and ambush it cannot see
values.focus_fire: being focused by the whole team
values.kiting: being kited by mobile ranged heroes
values.zoning: being walled out of the fight
values.macro_split: enemy split pushing while it fights
values.early_pressure: being pressured early before it scales
values.interruption: being interrupted or cancelled mid channel
values.global_pressure: global heroes and reactive rotations (Falstad, Dehaka, Nova ganks cancelled)
values.displacement: pulls, knockbacks and being separated from the team
values.reveal_or_aoe: stealth broken by detection or area damage

vulnerable_to.draft_use: Turns into a weakness map: add up what the comp is vulnerable to against what the enemy brings.

comp_affinity.question: Which comp archetypes does it fit?

values.poke_siege: long range chip damage and siege
values.dive_burst: jump on the backline and burst
values.sustain_teamfight: long fights with healing and shields
values.pick_catch: catch and kill targets before the fight

comp_affinity.draft_use: The archetype tally of the five picks tells you what the comp is trying to do and what it forgot.

bodies.question: How many bodies or players does the hero use?

values.two_player: two heroes on one team slot, two players (Cho and Gall)
values.multi_body: several bodies (The Lost Vikings, Rexxar with Misha)

bodies.draft_use: Two player and multi body heroes change how deaths and soak are counted.

owner_combos.name: Silence under a taunt, then burst
owner_combos.text: Stukov silences under the taunted target and the team bursts it with a ranged assassin whose damage minions and heroes cannot block. Fails if they can save the target: Anduin's pull, Medivh or Uther Divine Shield, Tyrael's invulnerability. Cleanses help them but the silence can still get kills.

owner_combos.name: CC tank then one target focus
owner_combos.text: Tyrande is often picked as the follow up to a CC tank to focus down one target with burst ranged damage or a melee assassin. She needs to auto attack safely to bring her heal back.

owner_combos.name: Orphea heroic reset behind big CC
owner_combos.text: Orphea's heroic resets when it hits a hero, which works best behind E.T.C. Mosh Pit or Leoric Entomb.

owner_combos.name: Sonya jumps in behind a CC chain
owner_combos.text: Sonya with Leap is a good partner for CC chain combos (Light bomb and other chains): high burst onto the backline.

owner_combos.name: Whitemane wants CC from the front line
owner_combos.text: Whitemane has little CC, so draft it in the tank and maybe the offlaner. She is weak to tanks that pull or separate her from the team: Stitches, Garrosh, Diablo.

owner_combos.name: Lucio wall riding gets stunned
owner_combos.text: Diablo can stun Lucio on walls while he is wall riding.

owner_combos.name: Lunara and the enemy healer
owner_combos.text: Lunara does great into low sustain healers like Uther because her poison on many people outruns his healing and mana. Healers like Brightwing heal through her steady damage.

owner_combos.name: Murky and quest stackers meet Ragnaros
owner_combos.text: Murky struggles against Ragnaros and others who can kill him for stacks or quests, or kill his W so it does not trigger.

owner_combos.name: Deathwing into a pick comp
owner_combos.text: Pick Deathwing when they have no percent damage hero and they have a pick comp: he cannot be stunned. A strong late pick, often taken in the 4 man as a damage dealer.

owner_combos.name: Hanzo and dive
owner_combos.text: High mobility dive heroes like Zeratul and Genji kill Hanzo easily. Minions and summons also block his abilities.

owner_combos.name: Sgt. Hammer and poke or dive
owner_combos.text: Sgt. Hammer is susceptible to dive and long range poke like Tassadar, Chromie and maybe Li-Ming.

owner_combos.name: Ragnaros on Tomb
owner_combos.text: On Tomb of the Spider Queen, clearing waves with Lava Wave loses the gems.
